NAME: PANHANDLE EASTERN PIPELINE CO
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: at 12:54pm pepl employee received call from a landowner that he could hear a leak and see vapor east of road n and south of 100 rd. at 1:00pm notified employees at olpe station to go to location and confirm leak and location. at 1:15pm the location and leak were confirmed and believed to be the 300l. at 1:17pm sent an employee to protect leak site and two employees to 300l west river header for isolation. at 1:23pm station valve 554-3 was closed. at 1:45pm a gauge was placed on 554-3 dsbo 642psi to confirm the 300l was leaking by pressure drop. at 1:47pm called lyon county dispatch and informed of the situation and location, was asked if assistance was needed, informed them that no assistance was needed at the time. at 1:48pm west river header valve 326w was closed, and at 1:55pm 516 w-1w was opened. at 2:10pm the station pressure was at 569 psi. at 2:17pm valve 516w-2w was opened. at 2:20pm station pressure was at 545 psi. at 2:28pm started blowdown. at 2:38pm 2 gate 300-400 crossover valve 302-e opened. at 2:39pm 2 gate 300-400 crossover valve 402-e opened. at 3:19pm isolated section was blown flat. on 4/11/2024 pipe was exposed, and leak identified as a cracked weld. a 44-foot pipe segment was cut out and replaced. a specimen was sent to the lab for evaluation and determination of cause. the lab report was completed on 11/1/2024 and found that the leak was caused by a combination of a preexisting delayed hydrogen crack on the internal pipe surface at the toe of the girth weld, the presence of a concentrated axial stress at the bottom of the pipe, and the exceedance of the girth weld's tensile strain capacity. the crack measured 34 inches long circumferentially along the bottom side of the girth weld.

NAME: MOUNTAINWEST PIPELINE, LLC
NARRATIVE: on 4/23/2024 williams reported an event to the nrc due to the total volume of gas release exceeding 3 mmscf. the total volume released that day was 17.76 mmscf totaling between two psv's on mainline 40 at the jl40-47 junction and green river meter station, but both released gas due to the same cause. at the time of the initial release operations was on site performing other work at the jl40-47 junction. at the time of the release there were two compressor stations that were down for maintenance, this left only one compressor station available in the area to move gas. an issue on the fuel control valve with the compressor that was running caused repeated shutdowns. these repeated shutdowns caused gas to backup on the system and pressures built up, ultimately causing the two psv's to lift on the mainline resulting in the gas release that was reported. the fuel valves were operated in safe mode to subvert a powered hour limitation set by solar to keep flow through on the line, however they had to be restarted every hour to maintain this.

NARRATIVE: on thursday, may 9th at approximately 1:25pm central time, emmet operations received a call from a third party about a possible line strike with a gas release. at 1:38pm, operations personnel confirmed that a third party had struck line sm-23 with a bulldozer causing a gas release. no one was injured and the gas did not ignite. an operations technician remained on site to monitor the release while one technician went to the upstream valve site and another technician mobilized to the downstream valve site. pressure at the time of the strike was 550psig; pressure was lowered to 350psig and monitored. the decision to monitor pressure was made to avoid significant outages to residential customers. once customer notifications were finalized, the pipeline was shunt in and blown down. a type b sleeve was installed over the defect and the pipeline was purged and returned to service on friday may 10th at approximately 4:40pm central time. the pipeline was struck by a third party logging company. the contractors working for the logging company did not complete a one call and were not authorized to perform work on the sm-23 right of way.

NARRATIVE: on june 15, 2024 at approximately 15:18 hours consumers energy gas control received notification of a damage at the winterfield storage field, marion township, michigan (osceola county). gas operations storage employees arrived onsite, confirmed the damage to w-905, and immediately shut-in the well line (wl-905). despite this, gas continued to release, indicating a loss of control. the well blowout contingency plan was then implemented. an investigation determined a contractor working on behalf of autumn vista dairy using a tractor and tanker to spread fertilizer, had backed into the wellhead, causing a release of gas, and damaging the wellhead and surface components, making the well incapable of isolation. upon determining the loss of control, personnel began evaluating the site to determine immediate needs and remained onsite until complete isolation of the well was achieved. consumers energy contacted cudd emergency well response (contractor), informing them of the incident and requesting assistance. both consumers energy and cudd mobilized at the site on june 16, 2024, to begin planning and implementing the well kill operation. two attempts to kill the well by suppressing it with liquids were unsuccessful, leading to a decision to use a vendor specialized blow out preventer (bop) to isolate and gain control of the well. on june 19, 2024, the wellbore was successfully isolated using a cudd blowout preventer and an asi-x packer was set and tested. cudd's bop was removed and replaced with a company bop. further action includes preparation for the complete well remediation, which will involve integrity diagnostic evaluations through logging and mechanical integrity testing. the well completion will also include installing new tubing, new api 6a surface equipment, and connecting pipeline. on july 24th, 2024, the well was logged with both gamma ray neutron and corrosion logging tools to validate downhole integrity before completing workover activities. this was the second time the well has been logged since its baseline assessment with zero notable changes. a new wellhead was then procured and installed in accordance with consumers energy procedures. the well was then completed with a 2-3/8-inch tubing string and new wellhead components and valves. the remaining work includes final pipeline connection to be completed by local operational and welding crews per their resource and project work plan. the final state of the well, once returned to service will include new api 6a wellhead and valves, replaced pipeline connection, updated downhole integrity logs, wellhead protection and signage. the final pipeline connection was completed by local operational and welding crews, and normal operations resumed on april 24, 2025. proper protection was also installed to safeguard the pipeline facilities from impact and excavation damage.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on december 29, 2024, batesville compressor station 63 on the tennessee gas pipeline (tgp) system experienced an esd event. gas control immediately contacted tgp operations at 01:45 cst. the operations team arrived on site at 2:05 cst and confirmed that gas was venting. the km technician identified valve 63-1s to be unexpectedly open and closed the valve and secured the gas release. the nrc was called at 3:04 cst by km personnel and the initial report was captured as received by 3:07 cst. a 48-hour nrc report was made to update the gas release volume to 49,399 mcf. initial investigation determined that lightning had struck the building protection system in compressor building "b" causing a loss of communication with the station controls. this loss of communication activated the tgp esd fail safe system. following an investigation regarding the valve operation, it was determined that the root cause of the issue was the failure of an obsolete actuator which resulted in the valve actuating to the open position rather than the intended closed position. the failure may have been attributed to internal debris or worn components within the actuator. upon further review of the esd system, it was concluded that six valves, including valve 63-1s, were equipped with esd activation that was not functionally required. as a result, an initiative was implemented to reconfigure these valves within the system to reduce the likelihood of mechanical failures.

facility would be shut in while repairs were made. the event was reported to the nrc at 11:09 cdt on 4/13/2025 since repairs could have exceeded $145,400 and we determined at that time that the event just below the pressure relief valve. the components of the assembly above the buckle rotated nearly 45� from vertical before a parting failure occurred. a bulge was progressively generated as the structure bent over, dissipating significant energy. micrographs show that the material exhibited significant plastic flow before failure. the overall plastic behavior of the material local to the bulge was consistent with mechanical testing results. mechanical testing shows an elongation of 32% to 36% and a reduction in area of 66% to 72%. subsize charpy v-notch test specimens (5 mm x 10 mm) NAME: EQT PRODUCTION
CAUSE_DETAILS: DEFECTIVE OR LOOSE TUBING OR FITTING
NARRATIVE: on august 28, 2025, there was a release of gas at the snapping turtle compressor station located in wind ridge, pa which is owned and operated by eqt production. chief inspector troy leek called the eqt environmental, health, & safety (ehs) hotline to report a gas release at the snapping turtle compressor station. upon arrival to the location, he observed the richhill township fire department (who had been dispatched to the location upon community notification), staged ~150' away on the shared access road. all contract personnel were mustered outside of the gate. the operations supervisor (john mincin) was notified. gas control was contacted to initiate a remote shut in of compressor unit #3, and operations personnel were dispatched to the site. upon examination, there was a tubing failure on a relief valve inside the station. upon evaluation, operations determined that no overpressure event occurred. pressure was ~917psi when the prv lifted. it was noted that the nut and ferrule of the 1/8" stainless steel tubing broke at the pilot which, by design, caused a loss of pressure to the main valve dome thus triggering a fail-open condition (caused the relief valve to lift). the suspected failure is excessive vibration, so new tubing was installed in a configuration that alleviated the vibration issue. eqt production examined other stations with similar tubing configurations as the failed tubing and found them to be fully operational for many years and without vibration issues. eqt production believes that this was an isolated event and particular to the relief valve tubing at this specific relief valve at snapping turtle compressor station.
